````text
1	=== README.md
2	# pstack
3	
4	i'm [poteto](https://x.com/poteto). i'm not a president or ceo, but i've worked with millions of lines of code at Meta, Netflix, and Cursor. i'm also on the react core team where i help build and maintain react compiler.
5	
6	there's a growing sense that ai writes too much slop code. i agree. i don't want to ship like a team of twenty slop artists. throughput without quality is not a goal i aspire to. if you want to go fast, go deep first. 
7	
8	**pstack is my answer.** these are the same skills i use every day to ship high quality code at Cursor. this turns cursor into a real engineering team. the goal is not to maximize loc, in fact it's the opposite. pstack helps you write less, but higher quality code.
9	
10	**pstack gives you fearless parallelism.** when you can go deep on one agent and trust it to write good, verifiable code, you can truly parallelize with confidence. start multiple agents up with `poteto-mode` and trust that they'll apply rigorous engineering principles to their work.
11	
12	**cursor gives you the best of all worlds.** every frontier model has its strengths and weaknesses. use any model with pstack. in fact, many of my skills use multi-model workflows to take advantage of each model's unique strengths.
13	
14	fork it. improve it. make it yours. PRs are welcome! 
15	
16	## install
17	
18	```bash
19	/add-plugin pstack
20	```
21	
22	in claude code:
23	
24	```bash
25	/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins
26	/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins
27	```
28	
29	claude code prefixes plugin commands and agents, so `/poteto-mode` is `/pstack:poteto-mode`. the [claude code adapter](./docs/harness/claude-code.md) maps every other cursor name. in claude code, `/pstack:setup-pstack` writes your model choices to `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`, and a step that needs a cursor-only feature, such as bugbot or automations, is skipped with a one-line note.
30	
31	claude code installs a generated copy of pstack, including this readme and the guide, from [`harness/pstack/`](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/harness/pstack) at the repository root. after you change pstack, run `node scripts/generate-pstack-harness-trees.mjs` from the repository root and commit the result. ci fails while the generated copy is out of date.
32	
33	## get started
34	
35	two steps:
36	
37	1. run [`/setup-pstack`](./skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md), pick a reasoning budget, and choose which models you want.
38	2. use [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) whenever you're doing anything that requires rigor.
39	
40	new here? the [pstack guide](./docs/guide/README.md) walks you through a first real task, from setup and prompting through verification and overnight runs. stuck, or unsure which skill fits? ask [`/poteto-help`](./skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md).
41	
42	that's it. the other skills are situational, and the mode skill uses them for you as needed. out of the box the mode splits work by model strength: code delegates (feature, refactoring, bug fix, perf, hillclimb) go to grok, while the hardest changes, prose, and judgment go to opus 5.5. the default panel is opus 5.5 / grok. [`/setup-pstack`](./skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) changes any of it.
43	
44	## usage
45	
46	use [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) at the start of a task. it reads your request, picks from a set of playbooks, and runs the other skills as the steps need them.
47	
48	pick `/poteto-mode` from the `/` menu before you type your task, so cursor attaches the skill to the message.
49	
50	### just use [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md)
51	
52	this skill is the main shortcut. i use it whenever i need the agent to do rigorous engineering work. it comes with twenty-three playbooks:
53	
54	```
55	/poteto-mode this pr has a subtle bug where the scroll drifts every 750ms even when idle. repro
56	first, then fix and verify.
57	```
58	
59	```
60	/poteto-mode i'm going to bed. land the stack even if ci flakes. i want everything merged by
61	morning.
62	```
63	
64	<details>
65	<summary>the twenty-three playbooks</summary>
66	
67	| playbook | for |
68	|---|---|
69	| [investigation](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/investigation.md) | a read-only question. how does x work, why was y built this way, are we sure. |
70	| [bug fix](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md) | reproduce a defect, root-cause it, and fix with runtime evidence. |
71	| [perf](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/perf-issue.md) | trace a measured slowness and improve it against a baseline. |
72	| [hillclimb](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/hillclimb.md) | sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target, looping hypotheses with before/after measurement and one commit per accepted win. |
73	| [runtime forensics](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/runtime-forensics.md) | diagnose a live symptom (leak, idle-cpu spin, glitch) from instrumentation. |
74	| [trace forensics](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/trace-forensics.md) | diagnose a captured profiling artifact (cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot). |
75	| [feature](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/feature.md) | new or changed behavior, built from a named data shape. |
76	| [refactoring](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/refactoring.md) | a behavior-preserving change to structure or shape. |
77	| [prototype](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/prototype.md) | a throwaway sketch to make a design or behavioral decision cheaply, or to settle an empirical fork by observing it. |
78	| [visual parity](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/visual-parity.md) | pixel-exact ui equivalence between two implementations. |
79	| [authoring a skill](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md) | writing or editing a SKILL.md. |
80	| [eval](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval.md) | test how a skill or prompt change affects agent behavior, blinded. |
81	| [babysit](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/babysit.md) | drive a pr or a stack to merge-ready: conflicts, review threads, ci. |
82	| [shipping](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/shipping.md) | independently verify a green stack, then land the contiguous verified run bottom-up through github by default or origin when available. |
83	| [autonomous run](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autonomous-run.md) | drive a long task to completion without stopping. |
84	| [orchestrate](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/orchestrate.md) | a standing project handed to one coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked prs, fleets of subagents. |
85	| [autopilot-full](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md) | run independent prs to merged with one owner per pr. a swarm verifies each code-ready head, and every later change to the patch gets a fresh check. |
86	| [autopilot-stack](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autopilot-stack.md) | build and verify one linear base-branch stack for the operator to review and land. |
87	| [session pickup](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/session-pickup.md) | resume or take over a prior agent's in-flight work. |
88	| [pause safely](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md) | suspend in-flight work cleanly so it can be resumed later. |
89	| [multi-phase plan](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md) | work that spans phases or stacked PRs. |
90	| [worktree cleanup](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md) | reclaim disk by pruning merged or abandoned worktrees and stale ios simulators, safety-gated. |
91	| [opening a pr](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) | open a ready pr from small ordered commits with a conventional commits title and a briefing-style body. invoked at the end of every other playbook. |
92	
93	</details>
94	
95	
96	
97	when invoked it:
98	
99	1. matches your task to a [playbook](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/) and opens a todo list whose first items are its steps, copied in verbatim.
100	2. routes to the other skills as the steps fire.
101	3. writes unslopped replies framed for the consumer and the maintainer.
102	
103	the full rules and playbooks live in [`skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md).
104	
105	to keep [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) on across turns, pick it from the `/` menu and press option+enter (mac) or alt+enter (windows) instead of enter. that makes it a [custom mode](https://cursor.com/docs/skills#using-a-skill-as-a-custom-mode), which cursor offers in the agents window and the cli. it stays in context every turn until you exit the mode. plain enter attaches it to one message only.
106	
107	[`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) works extremely well with cursor's `/loop` command. you can make cursor work for many hours without sacrificing rigor.
108	
109	## skills
110	
111	[`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) runs most of these for you when a step needs them (`how`, `why`, `architect`, `arena`, `swarm`, `interrogate`, `unslop`, `no-comments`, `technical-writing`, `tdd`, and the principles). the table below is for when you want one directly:
112	
113	```
114	/how do we cancel runs? do we have an n+1 when we look up every run to cancel?
115	```
116	
117	```
118	/interrogate review this pr.
119	```
120	
121	<details>
122	<summary>all skills</summary>
123	
124	| skill | use it when |
125	|---|---|
126	| [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) | default entry point for any non-trivial task. |
127	| [`/poteto-help`](./skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md) | you're new to pstack, or unsure which skill, playbook, or principle fits. finds out what you're trying to do, answers that part, and hands you a prompt to type. runs only when you type `/poteto-help`. |
128	| [`/in-your-own-words`](./skills/in-your-own-words/SKILL.md) | you want the agent to play back your goal and the problem before it starts. runs only when you type `/in-your-own-words`. |
129	| [`/sharpen`](./skills/sharpen/SKILL.md) | you want a task approached the way a top expert would, aimed at what you're really after, without overspecifying it or deciding your choices for you. |
130	| [`/how`](./skills/how/SKILL.md) | you want a walkthrough of how a subsystem works. |
131	| [`/why`](./skills/why/SKILL.md) | you want to know why something was built this way. discovers available MCPs at run time and queries each evidence category in parallel (source control, issue tracker, long-form docs, real-time chat, infra observability, error tracking, analytics warehouse). |
132	| [`/recall`](./skills/recall/SKILL.md) | you're starting or resuming work and want your recent context on a topic rebuilt from your own chat history and the shared record, handed back as a tight current-state brief. |
133	| [`/ketchup`](./skills/ketchup/SKILL.md) | you want what changed in this chat since your last message, in plain words and small visuals, with every item waiting on you listed and decidable from the reply alone, even when that makes the reply long. |
134	| [`/blast-radius`](./skills/blast-radius/SKILL.md) | you have a small-looking change and want to know what else it could break, with the one fact it's safe because of proven by running code, not asserted. |
135	| [`/architect`](./skills/architect/SKILL.md) | you're about to write code that crosses a function boundary and want the caller's usage, types, and module shape settled first. |
136	| [`/arena`](./skills/arena/SKILL.md) | you want N parallel attempts at the same thing, then to grab the best parts of each. |
137	| [`/swarm`](./skills/swarm/SKILL.md) | you want N parallel workers across different slices or races, then one aggregated report. |
138	| [`/interrogate`](./skills/interrogate/SKILL.md) | you have a diff and want different models to try to break it, including a strict code-quality lens. |
139	| [`/automate-me`](./skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) | you want your own `-mode` skill, drafted from how you've actually worked. |
140	| [`/make-bot-ui`](./skills/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md) | you want a page or dashboard whose buttons wake a Grok Bot over a webhook, including the sender-key handoff and Tailscale. |
141	| [`/setup-pstack`](./skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) | you want to pick which models pstack uses per role. detects your models and writes a config rule. |
142	| [`/reflect`](./skills/reflect/SKILL.md) | a long task landed and you want the recipe captured as a skill edit. |
143	| [`/correct`](./skills/correct/SKILL.md) | you keep correcting agents for the same mistakes. mines history for mistake classes, fixes each at the highest level that works (architecture, then types, lint, and ci, then tests, with docs last), and keeps a table pairing each rule with what enforces it. |
144	| [`/teach`](./skills/teach/SKILL.md) | you want to actually understand a change or subsystem, not just have it summarized. runs how + why and weaves one plain explanation, built up diagram by diagram. |
145	| [`/tdd`](./skills/tdd/SKILL.md) | you're fixing a bug and there's a cheap local test path. write the failing test first, then the fix. |
146	| [`/benchmark-checklist`](./skills/benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) | you ran a benchmark or measured a speedup or regression. vets the number (limiter, tuning, errors, repeat runs, end-to-end relevance) before you report or act on it. |
147	| [`/no-comments`](./skills/no-comments/SKILL.md) | strip comments before review; spawns Comment Sicko, fixes accepted findings, offers encodings for claimed constraints. |
148	| [`/typescript-best-practices`](./skills/typescript-best-practices/SKILL.md) | you're reading or editing typescript. grounds the type-system-discipline principle in syntax. |
149	| [`/figure-it-out`](./skills/figure-it-out/SKILL.md) | no bundled playbook fits. designs a rigorous, auditable playbook for the task. |
150	| [`/show-me-your-work`](./skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md) | you want a reviewable decision trail. logs decisions to a tsv you can commit. |
151	| [`/create-verification-skill`](./skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | your project has no scripted way to prove app behavior. generates a project-local verify skill with a feature map, for any language or platform. |
152	| [`/maintain-verification-skill`](./skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | your verify skill's feature map has drifted from the app. source wave + one live pass, at most one PR of proven corrections. |
153	| [`/create-formal-verification-skill`](./skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | tests can't reach the case that breaks a race, retry, state machine, parser, or unsafe code. verifies one property with the tool that fits and generates a project-local skill to recheck it on every change. |
154	| [`/maintain-formal-verification-skill`](./skills/maintain-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | code your formal verification covers has changed since it was last checked. updates the model, harness, or properties to match the code, reruns, and says whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. |
155	| [`/unslop`](./skills/unslop/SKILL.md) | you're cleaning up writing. removes AI tells. |
156	| [`/bro`](./skills/bro/SKILL.md) | you want the last message restated in plain human language, no jargon. |
157	| [`/technical-writing`](./skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) | layered doc standard (Diátaxis + Google developer style + STE + Global English) for docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, commit messages. |
158	
159	</details>

163	### examples
164	
165	mostly i type [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) at the start of a task and let it route to a playbook. the other skills fire as the steps need them. a few i reach for directly.
166	
167	
168	<details>
169	<summary>all the examples</summary>
170	
171	```
172	bug fix:           /poteto-mode this pr has a subtle bug where the scroll drifts every 750ms even
173	                   when idle. repro first, then fix and verify.
174	perf:              /poteto-mode a big list takes a second or two to load even though we virtualize.
175	                   run a cpu trace and tell me why.
176	feature:           /poteto-mode build a small feature behind a feature flag. verify it really works.
177	prototype:         /poteto-mode build two prototypes of the markdown renderer so we can compare.
178	                   spawn an agent for each.
179	multi-phase:       /poteto-mode open source these skills as a plugin. nothing internal leaks, work
180	                   in a temp dir, show me the dependency graph first.
181	overnight run:     /poteto-mode i'm going to bed. land the stack even if ci flakes. i want
182	                   everything merged by morning.
183	babysit:           /poteto-mode check on pr 123. anything outstanding?
184	visual parity:     /poteto-mode the row spacing is too tall when this flag is on. the second image
185	                   is correct. repro and fix until it matches.
186	figure it out:     /poteto-mode i'm stepping away. migrate every caller from the synchronous store
187	                   to the new async one, keeping behavior identical. i want to trust it was done
188	                   right when i'm back.
189	how:               /how do we cancel runs? do we have an n+1 when we look up every run to cancel?
190	why:               /why is this feature flag not on yet?
191	architect:         design this instrumentation to be high signal with no false positives. /architect
192	                   this first.
193	arena:             /arena take my prompt to the arena verbatim. i want to compare their proposals
194	                   with yours.
195	swarm:             /swarm check every package under packages/ against its check.sh. one worker per
196	                   package. one report.
197	interrogate:       /interrogate review this pr.
198	tdd:               /tdd implement
199	unslop:            can we unslop and tighten the new changes?
200	reflect:           /reflect that took too long. capture what we learned so the next run doesn't
201	                   repeat it.
202	correct:           /correct
203	show-me-your-work: /show-me-your-work keep a decision trail i can review when i'm back.
204	automate-me:       /automate-me
205	help:              /poteto-help which skill should i use to review this branch?
206	```
207	
208	</details>

210	## the `poteto-agent` and Comment Sicko subagents
211	
212	[`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) runs in the chat that receives it. that chat owns the playbook, the todo list, and every subagent spawn.
213	
214	pstack also ships [`subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`](./agents/poteto-agent.md) as the wrapper for delegates spawned during a run. it reads `poteto-mode` in full, including its inline principles index, before doing any work. substituting `generalPurpose` skips that read and drifts. do not spawn `poteto-agent` to run the playbook itself.
215	
216	[`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) and [`subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`](./agents/poteto-agent.md) route through the same wrapper.
217	
218	pstack also ships [Comment Sicko](./agents/comment-sicko.md), a read-only comment reviewer available as `subagent_type: "comment-sicko"`. usually invoke it through [`/no-comments`](./skills/no-comments/SKILL.md), not directly.
219	
220	## principles
221	
222	twenty-four short skills, one principle each. `poteto-mode` indexes them inline and reads that index at task start. the standalone files are there so other skills can reference a principle by name, and so the index can point at the full rule for each.
223	
224	<details>
225	<summary>all twenty-four principles</summary>
226	
227	| principle | group | rule |
228	|---|---|---|
229	| [laziness-protocol](./skills/principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md) | core | Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem. |
230	| [foundational-thinking](./skills/principle-foundational-thinking/SKILL.md) | core | Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious. |
231	| [redesign-from-first-principles](./skills/principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md) | core | Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on. |
232	| [attack-the-premise](./skills/principle-attack-the-premise/SKILL.md) | core | Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it. |
233	| [subtract-before-you-add](./skills/principle-subtract-before-you-add/SKILL.md) | core | Remove dead weight, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base. |
234	| [minimize-reader-load](./skills/principle-minimize-reader-load/SKILL.md) | core | Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope. |
235	| [outcome-oriented-execution](./skills/principle-outcome-oriented-execution/SKILL.md) | core | Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code. |
236	| [experience-first](./skills/principle-experience-first/SKILL.md) | core | Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones. |
237	| [exhaust-the-design-space](./skills/principle-exhaust-the-design-space/SKILL.md) | core | Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing. |
238	| [build-the-lever](./skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md) | core | Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun. |
239	| [model-the-domain](./skills/principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md) | architecture | Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals. |
240	| [boundary-discipline](./skills/principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md) | architecture | Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions. |
241	| [type-system-discipline](./skills/principle-type-system-discipline/SKILL.md) | architecture | Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas. |
242	| [make-operations-idempotent](./skills/principle-make-operations-idempotent/SKILL.md) | architecture | Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs. |
243	| [migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis](./skills/principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis/SKILL.md) | architecture | Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers. |
244	| [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](./skills/principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md) | architecture | Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant. |
245	| [prove-it-works](./skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md) | verification | Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'. |
246	| [fix-root-causes](./skills/principle-fix-root-causes/SKILL.md) | verification | Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate. |
247	| [sequence-verifiable-units](./skills/principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md) | verification | Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer. |
248	| [test-behavior-not-implementation](./skills/principle-test-behavior-not-implementation/SKILL.md) | verification | Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change. |
249	| [explain-the-number](./skills/principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) | verification | Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think. |
250	| [guard-the-context-window](./skills/principle-guard-the-context-window/SKILL.md) | delegation | Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads. |
251	| [never-block-on-the-human](./skills/principle-never-block-on-the-human/SKILL.md) | delegation | Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions. |
252	| [encode-lessons-in-structure](./skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md) | meta | Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text. |
253	
254	</details>
255	
256	## not shipped here
257	
258	a few things `poteto-mode` references but doesn't bundle:
259	
260	- `/deslop` and the `deslop` skill ship in the `cursor-team-kit` plugin.
261	- `control-cli` (for CLIs and TUIs) and `control-ui` (for browser, Electron, web) ship in `cursor-team-kit` too.
262	- `/create-skill` is a cursor built-in. cursor also ships a built-in `/autopilot` that watches a pr. inside `poteto-mode`, pr-status requests go to the [babysit playbook](./skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/babysit.md) instead.
263	
264	install `cursor-team-kit` alongside pstack if you want the full set.
265	
266	## why are there no planning skills?
267	
268	cursor already has a great plan mode which works great with pstack. but personally, i don't believe in planning. the best spec is code. if you do want to make a plan, [`/poteto-mode`](./skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md) covers it, but it's not a default. 
269	
270	## make it yours
271	
272	`poteto-mode` is my style. you may not want exactly that.
273	
274	type [`/automate-me`](./skills/automate-me/SKILL.md). it mines your recent transcripts, drafts a `<your-name>-mode` skill from how you've actually worked, and routes through pstack underneath. you keep pstack as the base and end up with your own routing skill alongside `poteto-mode`.
275	
276	models are configurable too. type [`/setup-pstack`](./skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md). it detects the models you have access to and writes a small always-applied rule mapping each role (code, judgment, the review panels) to a model. every skill reads it and falls back to sensible defaults when the rule is absent, so you override only what you want.
277	
278	when a default changes, a rule written before the change still pins the old default. delete those role lines, or delete the file, then run `/setup-pstack` again. a rerun keeps any role whose model differs from the default.
279	
280	## automations
281	
282	pstack also ships a dormant [benny automation pack](./automations/benny/). benny triages slack issue reports, then reproduces and fixes confirmed bugs with real ui evidence. its files are not registered as slash skills.
283	
284	to set it up, point cursor at [`FOR_AGENTS.md`](./automations/benny/FOR_AGENTS.md). setup copies the pack into the target repository at `.cursor/automations/benny/`, enables pstack there for shared skills, and keeps user configuration outside the copied pack. benny runs on cursor automations, so it is cursor-only.
285

343	=== docs/harness/claude-code.md
344	# pstack in Claude Code
345	
346	pstack skills use Cursor names. In Claude Code, read this file once per session, then map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<pstack>` means the folder that holds `skills/` and `docs/`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value the tool schema rejects.
347	
348	## Tools
349	
350	| Cursor | Claude Code |
351	| --- | --- |
352	| `Task` | `Agent` |
353	| `AskQuestion` | `AskUserQuestion`. In `-p` mode it is absent, so ask in plain text. |
354	| Open a todolist | Use `TodoWrite` if the session offers it. Otherwise keep the list in your reply and update it at each phase. |
355	| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | `Read` `<pstack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. The `Skill` tool refuses most pstack skills. When you tell the user to type it, write `/pstack:<name>`. |
356	| `Grep`, `Glob` | `Bash` with `rg` when the session has no `Grep` or `Glob`. |
357	
358	## Subagent fields
359	
360	| Cursor | Claude Code |
361	| --- | --- |
362	| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` |
363	| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `pstack:poteto-agent`, `pstack:comment-sicko` |
364	| `readonly: true` | `subagent_type: "Explore"`. It keeps `Bash`, so the brief also says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` afterward. |
365	| `readonly: false` | `general-purpose`. It keeps the session's MCP servers. |
366	| `environment: "cloud"` | `isolation: "worktree"`. Name the branch or commit the worker checks out. |
367	| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
368	| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
369	| `run_in_background: true` | Omit. Subagents run in the background by default and notify you when they finish. |
370	| `resume` | Spawn a new agent and paste the earlier result into its brief. |
371	| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the brief. |
372	
373	## Models
374	
375	| Cursor | Claude Code |
376	| --- | --- |
377	| `claude-<family>-<version>-<effort>[-fast]`, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` | `model: "opus"` and `effort: "xhigh"`. `model` takes only `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`. Drop `-fast`. |
378	| A `grok-*`, `gpt-*`, or other non-Claude slug | Omit `model` so the agent runs on the session model, and say so. |
379	| `auto` or `inherit-parent` | Omit `model`. |
380	| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`. Claude Code loads it into every new session, so its role lines are already in context. If they are not, read the file. If the file or the role's line is missing, use the skill's default slug. |
381	| A role value `<model> <effort>`, such as `opus high` | `model: "opus"` and `effort: "high"`. |
382	
383	## setup-pstack
384	
385	Claude Code loads every `.md` file in `~/.claude/rules/` into each new session, so `setup-pstack` writes its rule there. Follow its steps with these changes:
386	
387	- Detect. The detected models are the `model` values that the `Agent` tool schema lists, each with an effort from its `effort` values. Write a real model as `<model> <effort>`, such as `opus xhigh`. The effort is the last token, so the budget step works as written.
388	- Defaults. Map each default slug with the rows above: `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` is `opus xhigh`, and `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` is `inherit-parent`.
389	- Write. Write `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md` with no frontmatter, then the comment lines, the `# budget` line, and one line per role from step 5. Overwrite the whole file. Never put the role lines in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
390	
391	## Paths
392	
393	| Cursor | Claude Code |
394	| --- | --- |
395	| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/` |
396	| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | `~/.claude/plugins/`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` |
397	| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `CLAUDE.md`, or `AGENTS.md` when no `CLAUDE.md` exists. Claude Code never reads `.mdc` files. The model rule is the exception. See Models. |
398	| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `<pstack>/<path>` when that file exists. The plugin ships the skills, `docs/guide/`, and `README.md`. Read the local copy and never fetch it. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
399	| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl`. The slug is the workspace path with each `/` and `.` changed to `-`, so `/Users/you/proj` is `-Users-you-proj`. The newest `.jsonl` directly in that folder is the current session. Its `<session>/subagents/` folder holds subagent transcripts. Read only this workspace's folder. |
400	
401	## Cursor-only features
402	
403	Claude Code has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in Claude Code: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, such as a URL or a key, leave a placeholder and name it in the line.
404	
405	| Cursor | Claude Code |
406	| --- | --- |
407	| Cursor Automations: routines, `update_state` routine calls, `api2.cursor.sh/automations` webhooks, routine wakes, and `SendToUser` secret requests | Skip with the line. |
408	| Bugbot | Bugbot comments on a GitHub PR are ordinary review threads, so triage them with the forge command that the step gives. Skip a step that starts, waits for, or configures Bugbot when the PR has no Bugbot check or comment. |
409	| Cursor cloud agents | `environment: "cloud"` maps to a worktree, as in Subagent fields. Skip a step that needs the cloud agent itself, such as its dashboard status or its own machine. |
410	| A built-in PR tool | Use the forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. That is not a skip, so write no line. |

433	=== skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md
434	---
435	name: setup-pstack
436	description: Configure which models pstack uses per role and at what reasoning budget. Detects your available models and writes an always-applied rule that overrides the skill defaults. Use for /setup-pstack, "configure pstack models", "pstack budget", or changing pstack's model choices.
437	---
438	
439	# Setup pstack
440	
441	Write `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, an always-applied rule that sets pstack's model per role.
442	
443	## Steps
444	
445	### 1. Detect available models
446	
447	Enumerate the model slugs you can pass to a `Task` subagent in this session. That is the dependable source. If Cursor also exposes a models API or CLI that lists the user's entitled models, prefer it for completeness. If you cannot detect any, ask the user to paste the slugs they have access to. Never write a real slug you have not confirmed is available. The aliases `inherit-parent` and `auto` are always valid even though they are not detected slugs.
448	
449	### 2. Load current state
450	
451	The default role-to-model mapping is the rule shape shown in step 5 below. If `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` already exists, read it and treat its `# budget` line and its role values as the current choices. Otherwise start from those defaults. A line whose role is not in step 5, such as `how critics`, is from a retired role. Drop it.
452	
453	### 3. Budget, map, and confirm
454	
455	**(a) Ask for a budget.** Prefer AskQuestion over free text. Offer these four options with these exact labels, and name the current budget when the rule records one. With no rule, say that `large` matches the skill defaults.
456	
457	- `unlimited — max reasoning`
458	- `large — xhigh reasoning`
459	- `medium — high reasoning`
460	- `small — medium reasoning`
461	
462	**(b) Apply it.** Build the working table from the skill defaults, and on a re-run keep any role you changed by family, list, or alias (`inherit-parent`, `auto`). `unlimited`, `large`, `medium`, and `small` set the effort token of every real slug, panel entries included, to `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, or `medium`. The effort token is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`, on the ladder `max` > `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. If the result is not a detected slug, use the same family's detected slug with the highest effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `unlimited` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` into `claude-opus-5-5-max`. Grok slugs top out at `xhigh`, so under `unlimited` the fallback puts Grok at `xhigh` and keeps `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` as it is. `large` keeps both defaults. `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium` and `grok-4.7-medium-fast`.
463	
464	**(c) Show the roles and confirm.** Show every role with its model, marking any real slug not in the detected set as needing a choice. Also list each line step 2 dropped. Ask whether to accept as-is or change specific roles, offering the detected models plus `inherit-parent` and `auto` (both mean: this role runs on the parent chat model, which is how Auto users stay on Auto) as the options. Prefer AskQuestion over free text. For panel roles (arena runners, architect runners, interrogate reviewers) the value is a list, and one subagent runs per entry, alias entries included, so the list length sets the count. `arena cross-judge pool` is also a list, but Arena selects one value from it whose model family differs from the parent's when possible. `swarm workers` is the default model for every worker unless a race or comparison assigns another model per arm.
465	
466	### 4. Validate
467	
468	Every real slug written must be in the detected set. `inherit-parent` and `auto` always pass. If a chosen real slug is not available, stop and ask again.
469	
470	### 5. Write the rule
471	
472	Write `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` with `alwaysApply: true`, a `# budget` line with the chosen label and its target effort, and one line per role, using the same labels poteto-mode uses. Overwrite the whole file so re-runs stay idempotent. Shape:
473	
474	```
475	---
476	description: pstack per-role model choices (overrides skill defaults)
477	alwaysApply: true
478	---
479	# pstack model configuration. One line per role. Delete a line to fall back to the skill default.
480	# `inherit-parent` or `auto` as a value: the role runs on the parent chat model (omit Task `model`). Alias entries in a panel list still count toward its fan-out.
481	# budget: large (xhigh)
482	feature, refactoring: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
483	bug-fix: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
484	perf-issue: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
485	hillclimb: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
486	judgment and prose: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh
487	hardest tasks: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh
488	how explorer: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
489	how explainer: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh
490	why investigators: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
491	why synthesizer: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh
492	reflect tooling: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
493	reflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh
494	arena runners: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh, grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
495	arena cross-judge pool: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh, grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
496	swarm workers: grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
497	architect runners: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh, grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
498	interrogate reviewers: claude-opus-5-5-xhigh, grok-4.7-xhigh-fast
499	```
500	
501	### 6. Confirm
502	
503	Tell the user the rule was written and that it applies to new sessions. Re-running this skill updates it.
504	
505	### 7. Offer a verification skill (optional)
506	
507	Check whether the project has a way to drive the real app for proof (a `verify-*` skill, or an existing harness). If not, offer once: "want a project-local verification skill, so agents can drive the app the way a user does and prove changes work? I can generate one with /create-verification-skill." On yes, invoke `/create-verification-skill` (resolves wherever pstack is installed: workspace, user, or plugin). On no, move on without pushing.
508	
509	### 8. Offer a formal verification skill (optional)
510	
511	Check whether the project already has a formal verification skill (a project skill that runs a model checker, a proof, or another verifier against the code). If not, offer once: "want a formal verification skill, so agents can prove a key property of your code holds in every case in scope, not only the cases tests reach? I can generate one with /create-formal-verification-skill." On yes, invoke `/create-formal-verification-skill` (resolves wherever pstack is installed: workspace, user, or plugin). On no, move on without pushing.
512	=== skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md
513	---
514	name: poteto-mode
515	description: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.
516	disable-model-invocation: true
517	icon: crown
518	color: yellow
519	---
520	
521	# Poteto mode
522	
523	Bundled skills live at `../<name>/SKILL.md` from this file, so put this file's absolute path in every `poteto-agent` prompt.
524	
525	## Non-negotiables
526	
527	The Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.
528	
529	Remaining triggers:
530	
531	- Nontrivial change, architecture decision, or "are we sure?" → the **how** skill.
532	- About to `AskQuestion` on a "which approach", "how should I", or "what should this do" fork → classify it before you ask. If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer. Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide. If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch. Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle. Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer. Under the grant, for a call only the operator can make, apply a default, report it with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead. The operator answers in their own words. Never give a shorthand token to type back. Gates the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.
533	- Any code → name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.
534	- Code crossing a function boundary → the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.
535	- Parallel fan-out → the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.
536	- Contested design → the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.
537	- Nontrivial multi-step → write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).
538	- Any prose surface, your reply to the user included → the **unslop** skill. Write the reply per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **create-skill** skill (Cursor's built-in for authoring SKILL.md files).
539	- Docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages → the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`).
540	- Before commit → the `deslop` skill from the `cursor-team-kit` plugin (`/deslop`).
541	- Before review → the **no-comments** skill (`/no-comments`).
542	- Shipping UI / IDE / CLI → the matching control skill. `cursor-team-kit` publishes `control-cli` (CLIs and TUIs) and `control-ui` (browser / Electron / web UIs). For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself. Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.
543	- Running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured → the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.
544	- Any PR-status request ("babysit this", "get it green", "address the bugbot comments", and most often "check on PR X" or "anything outstanding on X") → the **Babysit** playbook (`playbooks/babysit.md`), not Cursor's built-in babysit skill, whose description matches the same words. Never triggered by merely opening a PR. Declare its mode before polling. The playbook's step 1 owns the request-to-mode mapping. Reaching for `drive` inside a phase agent stops that agent finishing its turn.
545	- Asked to land or ship a green stack → the **Shipping** playbook (`playbooks/shipping.md`). Green is not safe. Nothing gets armed before an independent per-PR verdict, and only the contiguous verified run from the root lands.
546	- Bugbot or the agentic security review commented → skeptical posture. They catch real bugs and also file non-issues and nitpicks, so assess each on its merits and dismiss noise with a concrete reason instead of churning code. Triage fix / dismiss / ask per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.
547	- Broken skill mid-task → fix it in its own PR. Don't block. Don't silently work around it.
548	- Long, autonomous, or multi-phase work, or any task the user steps away from to review later ("going to bed", "trust it when i'm back", "/loop until X") → a decision trail via the **show-me-your-work** skill. Commit it when stakes need an auditable record. Keep it local otherwise.
549	
550	## Principles
551	
552	Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies. Each leaf is the **principle-<title>** skill, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its name.
553	
554	**Core**
555	
556	- **Laziness Protocol.** Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
557	- **Foundational Thinking.** Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
558	- **Redesign from First Principles.** Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
559	- **Attack the Premise.** Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.
560	- **Subtract Before You Add.** Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
561	- **Minimize Reader Load.** Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
562	- **Outcome-Oriented Execution.** Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.
563	- **Experience First.** Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.
564	- **Exhaust the Design Space.** A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.
565	- **Build the Lever.** Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.
566	
567	**Architecture**
568	
569	- **Model the Domain.** Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.
570	- **Boundary Discipline.** Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
571	- **Type System Discipline.** Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
572	- **Make Operations Idempotent.** Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
573	- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs.** Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.
574	- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State.** Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.
575	
576	**Verification**
577	
578	- **Prove It Works.** After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".
579	- **Fix Root Causes.** Debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.
580	- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.
581	- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation.** Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.
582	- **Explain the Number.** Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.
583	
584	**Delegation**
585	
586	- **Guard the Context Window.** Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.
587	- **Never Block on the Human.** Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.
588	
589	**Meta**
590	
591	- **Encode Lessons in Structure.** You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.
592	
593	## Autonomy
594	
595	**Just do it.** Use any MCP tool. Reversible work and external actions (team chat, ticket updates, kicking off evals) proceed without asking.
596	
597	**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.
598	
599	**Session overrides:** "Don't stop" / "going to bed" / "run until done" / "be fully autonomous" → keep going.
600	
601	**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say "this doesn't earn its place" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.
602	
603	## Subagents
604	
605	**Use `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"` for any subagent you spawn inside a playbook step** (code-writing delegates, ad-hoc helpers). The chat that receives `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook. Never spawn a `poteto-agent` to run the playbook itself. Routed workflow skills (`how`, `why`, `interrogate`, `reflect`, `swarm`) set their own `subagent_type` for diverse-model review. Respect what the skill prescribes, don't override to `poteto-agent`.
606	
607	**Defaults for every `Task` call.** `run_in_background: true`, agent mode (readonly strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, explicit model per role (configurable via `/setup-pstack`. Defaults `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` for code, `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` for prose and judgment). Code delegates tier by difficulty. The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest judgment model (`claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model. Per-role lines in the `/setup-pstack` rule override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent chat model (omit Task `model`). Each code playbook's configured model comes from its line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), and the hardest changes read `hardest tasks`. Prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`.
608	
609	**Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, start from the role's line or default and pick the reasoning level and speed the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level, xhigh by default. Raise it one step, up to max, for the hardest or subtlest work. Lower it one step for judgment and two or more steps for routine work. Use fast mode only when the job is urgent, meaning CI or trunk is red or a person is blocked on the result right now. Otherwise use standard speed, the same slug without `-fast`. Verification is the exception and stays on the `swarm workers` model and speed (`grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` by default). Change only the effort level and whether the slug is fast, and keep the family the role names, so a diverse panel stays diverse. If the family has no slug at that level and speed, use its nearest slug. A role on `auto` or `inherit-parent` stays on the parent model. If the Task tool rejects the adjusted slug, do not try another adjusted slug. Use the role's line or default and say so.
610	
611	You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Agreement is high-signal.
612	
613	**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a "done" summary.
614	
615	## Writing the reply
616	
617	Write the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.
618	
619	- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.
620	- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence ("`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC handlers") and a bold section header as its own sentence ("**Verification.** End to end via CDP").
621	- **A colon as a mid-sentence connector is also out** (unslop rule 14). A colon before a list is fine.
622	- **Terse is not an excuse to drop content.** Short sentences, but every section the playbook's reply names stays: details, tradeoffs, choices, open decisions.
623	- **Frame impact for the consumer and the maintainer.** Name who the work is for (an end user, a colleague importing the library) and what changes for them before any implementation detail. Then what the next engineer who owns this code inherits. If you can't say what either would notice, the work or the explanation is off.
624	- **Never fabricate a link, citation, or transcript reference.** Link only artifacts you produced or read this session.
625	- **Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence.** Measured, inferred, or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Never hand the human a check you could run.
626	
627	Every playbook ends with a reply written this way, PR link as `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>`. Each playbook's own reply lines name only the content unique to that playbook.
````

import { dirname, join, posix, relative } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const ROOT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const PSTACK = join(ROOT, "pstack");
const SKILLS = join(PSTACK, "skills");
// Outside pstack/ so Cursor, which copies the whole plugin folder, does not install this tree too.
const OUT = join(ROOT, "harness", "pstack");
const TREE = "claude-code";
const ADAPTER = "docs/harness/claude-code.md";
const GUIDE = "docs/guide";
const MANIFESTS = ["plugin.json", ".claude-plugin/plugin.json"];
const COMMAND = "node scripts/generate-pstack-harness-trees.mjs";
const GITHUB = "https://github.com/cursor/plugins";
const LINK = /\]\(([^)\s]+)\)/g;
const README = `# pstack harness tree

This folder is generated from \`pstack/skills\`, \`pstack/agents\`, \`pstack/${GUIDE}\`, \`pstack/${ADAPTER}\`, \`pstack/README.md\`, \`pstack/LICENSE\`, and \`pstack/plugin.json\`. Do not edit it by hand.

Cursor uses \`pstack/\` directly, and Claude Code installs \`${TREE}/\`. The tree leaves out the rest of \`pstack/\`, such as \`pstack/automations\` and \`pstack/assets\`. A relative link to a pstack file that the tree leaves out points at that file on GitHub \`main\` instead.

After editing those sources, run \`${COMMAND}\` from the repository root and commit the result.
`;

];

function walk(dir) {
  return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((name) => {
    if (name === ".DS_Store" || name === "node_modules") return [];
    const path = join(dir, name);
    return statSync(path).isDirectory() ? walk(path) : [path];
  });

The search turned up several ports of pstack's poteto-mode to Codex and OpenCode, though no single authoritative "port skills" page. I dropped the "OR" from your query since the search tool doesn't support operators.

- **Upstream:** The original is a Cursor skill stack by Lauren Tan (poteto), and the router skill is poteto-mode. It picks one of 23 playbooks and hands the coding to subagents before it asks for evidence that the work is done.
- **Ystack (Go7hic):** A portable fork that maps capability verbs to Claude Code, Codex, Droid, OpenCode, Cursor, and unknown Agent Skills hosts. Install is via npx skills add Go7hic/ystack -g -s '*' -y, which keeps the full pack.
- **Uni-pstack (kashyab12):** A Codex-oriented port. Its poteto-mode skill says that in Claude Code, Codex CLI workers are launched via the installed pstack skill spawn-codex-worker script or direct codex exec, and it sets Codex models in place of the upstream Claude defaults.
- **potetos-for-everyone (TheOnlyFusionCube):** A multi-platform bridge. For Codex, it discovers user skills from ~/.agents/skills/, and you clone or symlink the shared skill tree and Codex command prompts. Its README also says subagents must be enabled in ~/.codex/config.toml.
- **Sourceforge mirror:** Describes pstack as supporting Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only installations.

I didn't find a dedicated OpenCode port guide in these results; OpenCode appears only as an adapter target in ystack and as a listed integration on everydev.ai. Versions and maintenance status of these projects weren't verified.

# pstack: evaluation → catalog-only entry

## Context

The user asked whether to vendor pstack (`cursor/plugins/pstack`, by Lauren Tan / poteto, MIT,
v0.15.28). They also asked how it works outside Cursor and whether we would need to adapt it.
**Decision (user): catalog only. Nothing goes into `vendor.yaml`.**

Evaluation findings (from upstream, 2026-10-19):

- **Size and coupling.** 56 SKILL.md files: the `poteto-mode` router with 23 playbooks, 24 `principle-*`
  leaf skills, and 2 agents (`poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko`), plus TS/Bun scripts (`orch`, `watch-pr`).
  Skills read siblings via `../<name>/SKILL.md` and an adapter at `../../docs/harness/claude-code.md`.
  Our per-skill sync (`scripts/sync-vendor.sh`) does not copy `docs/`, so vendored copies would ship broken links.
- **Churn.** Several commits a day (5 commits on 2026-10-18/19 alone). Weekly `chore/vendor-sync` PRs would be noisy.
- **Claude Code is already handled upstream.** `harness/pstack/claude-code/` is generated by
  `scripts/generate-pstack-harness-trees.mjs` and enforced by CI. Install with
  `/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins` and then `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`. Commands become
  `/pstack:<name>`. The adapter maps `Task`→`Agent`, `readonly`→`Explore`, `cloud`→`isolation: worktree`,
  and `.mdc` rules→`~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`. Non-Claude model slugs (the default Grok code role) fall back to the
  session model. Cursor-only features (Automations, Bugbot, cloud agents, the benny pack) are skipped with a one-line note.
  We do not need our own adaptation.
- **Codex / OpenCode / Pi / Gemini.** Upstream ships nothing official. Community ports exist, all MIT, small, and behind upstream:
  `Go7hic/ystack` (★16, last push 2026-08-09; capability-verb mapping for Claude Code/Codex/Droid/OpenCode/Cursor),
  `TheOnlyFusionCube/potetos-for-everyone` (★16, 2026-09-10; Claude Code/Pi/Codex/Gemini, built on v0.15.0+),
  `kashyab12/uni-pstack` (★0, 2026-07-10; Codex-first).
- **Picker pollution and conflicts.** Generic names (`tdd` clashes with `engineering-fundamentals/tdd`, plus `how`, `why`, `teach`,
  `recall`, `correct`, `bro`). `disable-model-invocation: true` may not be honored by every `npx skills` target.
- **Only three skills work on their own** (`unslop`, `benchmark-checklist`, `blast-radius`). They have no sibling or adapter refs.
  These are the first candidates if we revisit.

## Changes

   `| poteto's pstack | [cursor/plugins/pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) | \`evaluated\` | <reason> |`.

## 結論：不收錄成 vendor skill，只在 catalog 加一筆 `evaluated` 條目

已經 commit 在 `main`（`b06694f`），還沒 push。改了 4 個檔案，中英文版本都有：`docs/catalog/skill-collections{,.zh-TW}.md` 和 `docs/catalog/domains/agent-harness{,.zh-TW}.md`。`make validate` 通過，`make docs-build` 也成功，沒有壞掉的連結。`vendor.yaml`、`marketplace.json` 和 `skills/` 都沒動。

### 為什麼不 vendor
- **太大，而且 skill 之間互相依賴。** 總共 56 個 SKILL.md：`poteto-mode` 這個 router 加 23 個 playbook、24 個 `principle-*`、2 個 agent，還有 TS/Bun 腳本。skill 會用 `../<name>/SKILL.md` 讀旁邊的 skill，也會讀 `../../docs/harness/claude-code.md`。我們的 `sync-vendor.sh` 是一個 skill 一個 skill 地同步，不會複製 `docs/`，所以 vendor 進來的 skill 裡這些連結會失效。
- **更新太頻繁。** 現在是 v0.15.28，光 10/18 到 10/19 就有 5 個 commit。每週的 sync PR 會很吵。
- **會污染 picker。** 它的 `tdd` 和我們 `engineering-fundamentals/tdd` 同名。`how`、`why`、`teach`、`recall`、`bro` 這類名字太通用。另外 `disable-model-invocation: true` 不一定每個 agent 都會遵守。

### Cursor 以外的使用體驗
- **Claude Code：不需要我們自己改，官方已經做好了。** `cursor/plugins` 用腳本生成一份 `harness/pstack/claude-code/`，CI 會檢查它有沒有跟上原版。安裝方式：`/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins`，再 `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`。指令名稱會變成 `/pstack:poteto-mode`。官方的 adapter 負責把 Cursor 的名稱對應過來：
  - `Task` 對應 `Agent`，`readonly` 對應 `Explore`，cloud agent 對應 worktree。
  - 模型設定寫到 `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`。
  - 原本預設用 Grok 的角色，在 Claude Code 會改用目前 session 的模型。
  - Bugbot、Automations 這類 Cursor 專屬功能會跳過，並留一行說明。
- **Codex、OpenCode、Pi、Gemini：官方沒有支援，但已經有人做了移植，跟你猜的一樣。** 三個都是 MIT 授權、規模都很小，也都比原版落後：
  - [Go7hic/ystack](https://github.com/Go7hic/ystack)：★16，最後更新 8/9，支援範圍最廣。
  - [potetos-for-everyone](https://github.com/TheOnlyFusionCube/potetos-for-everyone)：★16，最後更新 9/10。
  - [uni-pstack](https://github.com/kashyab12/uni-pstack)：★0，以 Codex 為主。

### 如果之後要重新評估
只有 `unslop`、`benchmark-checklist`、`blast-radius` 這三個不依賴其他 skill 或 adapter，可以單獨挑出來 vendor。這點已經寫進 catalog 的備註。我沒有加 `P?` TODO；需要的話可以補，status 會改成 `deferred`。

資料來源：[cursor/plugins/pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack)、[Claude Code 版本](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/harness/pstack/claude-code)，以及 [skills.sh 上的 uni-pstack](https://www.skills.sh/kashyab12/uni-pstack/pstack)、[skills.sh 上的 ystack](https://www.skills.sh/go7hic/ystack/poteto-mode)。flaviocopes 的文章回傳 403 讀不到；兩支 YouTube 影片和 Gemini 分享連結也沒看。
